test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 1 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the Election Commission of India?

options.text: It is Constituted every four years.
It is a Permanent constitutional body.
It is Constituted every six years.
It is Constituted every five years.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a Permanent constitutional body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Election Commission of India is established by the Constitution of India under Article 324.
 
• It is a permanent body, which means it is not dissolved after a certain period and continues to function perpetually.
 
• The main responsibility of the Election Commission is to conduct free and fair elections in India at both the central and state levels.
 
• The Commission consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, appointed by the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Body:**

 
 
• A constitutional body is an organization established by the Constitution of a country.
 
• It derives its powers, functions, and responsibilities from the Constitution itself, making it an integral part of the country's governance framework.
 
 
 
• **Article 324:**
 
 
• Article 324 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Election Commission of India.
 
• It vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner:**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is the head of the Election Commission of India.
 
• The CEC is appointed by the President of India and holds office for a term of six years or until reaching the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Election Commission:**
 
 
• Conducting elections for the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President in India.
 
• Preparing and updating the electoral rolls to ensure eligible voters are registered.
 
• Monitoring and regulating the conduct of political parties and candidates to ensure free and fair elections.
 
• Implementing the Model Code of Conduct during elections to maintain order and fairness.
